1.e4 e5 2.f4 exf4 3.Bc4 Qh4+ 4.Kf1 Ne7 5.strategy: Builds a central pawn pair and opens the c1-bishop's diagonal on f4, which only the g-pawn and the queen guard. White accepts the king on f1 for active play, and Black must now find a way to keep the pawn without losing time.

Reaches the position of the other move order: the bishop takes the long diagonal and pressures the d4 pawn, and the knight on e7 can head for g6 to help hold f4. But White can now play the g3 pawn sacrifice in a version that suits White better.
